comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation is subject to an FDIC special assessment to recover losses from the closures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, with quarterly collections beginning in Q2 2024; the accrual was $1.7 billion as of December 31, 2024, compared to $2.1 billion in 2023, and the liability amount may change based on the FDIC's updated loss estimates.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America disclose exposure to the FDIC special assessment imposed to recover Deposit Insurance Fund losses following the closures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank. A key difference is the timing of cash collections relative to the accrual recognition: JPM recognized a $2.9 billion assessment in Q4 2023 and an increase of $725 million in Q1 2024, whereas BAC began its quarterly collections in Q2 2024, resulting in a year-end accrual of $1.7 billion for 2024 compared to $2.1 billion in 2023. Both firms note that the final liability amounts may fluctuate based on the FDIC's revised loss estimates.

sentences.text: (c) The first quarter of 2024 included an increase of $725 million to the FDIC special assessment reflecting the FDIC's revised estimate of Deposit Insurance Fund losses.
The fourth quarter of 2023 included the $2.9 billion FDIC special assessment.

In 2023, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) issued a final rule to impose a special assessment to recover certain estimated losses to the Deposit Insurance Fund (DIF) arising from the closures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank.
As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, the Corporation's accrual for its estimated share of the FDIC special assessment was $1.7 billion and $2.1 billion.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citi recorded $203 million and $1,706 million in Other operating expenses for the years ended 2024 and 2023, respectively, related to the FDIC's final rule implementing a special assessment to recover uninsured deposit losses from the failures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, reflected in Corporate/Other in All Other.
comparisons.comparison: Citi and JPMorgan Chase both report specific expense line items related to the FDIC special assessment for uninsured deposit losses from the SVB and Signature Bank failures. Citi recorded $1,706 million in 2023 and $203 million in 2024. In contrast, JPM reported a much larger $2.9 billion assessment in Q4 2023 and a $725 million increase in Q1 2024. The disparity in reported expenses highlights differences in the magnitude and timing of charges incurred by the peers during the same period.
